payload.label: Class A simple reaction times (seconds), n = 15, sorted

stimuli.alt_text: Fifteen sorted reaction times in seconds for Class A, ranging from 0.20 to 0.70 seconds.

payload.label: Class B simple reaction times (seconds): five-number summary, n = 15

stimuli.alt_text: Class B five-number summary: minimum 0.24, Q1 0.30, median 0.38, Q3 0.48, maximum 0.55 seconds.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the Class A data, calculate the median reaction time and the interquartile range (IQR). Show the quartiles you use.

criteria.description: Reports the median as the 8th sorted value, 0.33 seconds.
Reports Q1 = 0.26 and Q3 = 0.40, giving IQR = 0.14 seconds.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the 1.5 x IQR rule to determine whether the Class A data contain any outliers. Show the boundaries you use and identify any outliers.

criteria.description: Computes 1.5 x IQR = 0.21 and the fences: upper = Q3 + 0.21 = 0.61, lower = Q1 - 0.21 = 0.05.
Identifies 0.70 as an outlier because it exceeds the upper fence 0.61, and states no value falls below 0.05, so it is the only outlier.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe the distribution of Class A reaction times. Address shape, center, spread, and any unusual features in context.

criteria.description: Describes the shape as skewed to the right (or not symmetric), referencing the high tail / value 0.70.
Reports center using the median, about 0.33 seconds, in context of reaction times.
Reports spread with a resistant measure (IQR = 0.14 s) or range, and names the outlier at 0.70 s as an unusual feature.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The Class B five-number summary is given. Compare the two classes' reaction-time distributions and justify a claim about which class tended to react faster.

criteria.description: Compares centers: Class A median 0.33 s is less than Class B median 0.38 s, so Class A tended to react faster.
Compares variability using IQR: Class A IQR 0.14 s is less than Class B IQR 0.18 s (0.48 - 0.30), so Class B is more variable; uses a resistant measure given Class A's outlier.
States a justified comparative claim in context: Class A reacted faster on average, acknowledging Class B's greater spread and Class A's high outlier.

accessibility.accommodation_notes: Data provided as a sorted numeric list and a five-number-summary table, both with alt_text. Responses are typed math and typed text; no student-produced graph is required, consistent with the frq-practices-3-4 archetype.
